maya: FYI support ticket #12345 — customer org_acme_media reports daily usage CSV and console daily chart are shifted by one day for CET users. They say events at 23:30 CET show up under the previous day in the CSV and in the dashboard.
maya: Example (export snippet):
```
date,start_ts_iso,count
2025-02-14,2025-02-14T22:45:00Z,12
2025-02-15,2025-02-15T23:30:00Z,5
```
They expect the 23:30 CET row to be on 2025-02-15 local day, but it landed on 2025-02-14. Org timezone: Europe/Paris. Customer is saying billing looks wrong.
jack: @maya thanks — can you paste the export file (or a snippet) and the org id? Also did they use the web console export or the API?

maya: Export was from Console > Usage > Export CSV. org id (masked): org_acme_media. Attached a slightly larger CSV (pasted below) — you can see timestamps are in UTC but day column appears to be UTC-truncated.
```
org_id,event_ts_utc,event_type
org_acme_media,2025-02-15T22:30:00Z,token_gen
org_acme_media,2025-02-15T23:15:00Z,token_gen
```
When viewed in CET (UTC+1) those map to 2025-02-16 early morning local, but CSV aggregates show them on previous day.
samir: Likely cause: daily aggregation step/date_trunc is being run in UTC and we're not converting to org's tz before truncation. Our current query snippets use `DATE_TRUNC('day', ts)` (BigQuery/Postgres-style) without `AT TIME ZONE` or equivalent. We store event timestamps in UTC and then `date_trunc`—that will produce UTC day boundaries.
Suggested quick check: run a query with `DATE(ts AT TIME ZONE 'Europe/Paris')` and compare counts.
Example (pseudo-SQL):
```sql
SELECT org_id, DATE(TIMESTAMP_SECONDS(event_ts) AT TIME ZONE org_tz) as local_day, COUNT(*)
FROM events
WHERE org_id = 'org_acme_media' AND event_ts BETWEEN X AND Y
GROUP BY 1,2;
```
If that flips counts to the expected dates then ingestion/truncation is the bug.
elaine: How many customers hit so far? Is billing actually charged differently or just display/export issues? We need scope and customer impact (refund risk).
maya: So far two escalations: org_acme_media and org_velvet. One reported an overage invoice because their daily cap was based on counts that were shifted into the prior day when they expected them on the next. So billing/customer impact = yes for at least one customer.
jack: I'm filing an internal issue and marking P1. Creating RI-7834 in tracker and assigning @samir. Link: https://issues.internal/RI-7834. @samir can you take ownership? Also please include rollback/backfill plan and a mitigation for support to give customers.
samir: I can take it. Quick mitigation options: (1) change export UI to include a dropdown to select timezone (or explicit note "exports use UTC"), (2) change ETL to compute `local_day` using org timezone and use that for aggregates/exports, and (3) backfill corrected local_days for last 7 days (one-time job). I'll prepare a patch to ETL+export layer.
Hotfix plan: patch ingestion/aggregation to write a `local_day` column using org_tz at aggregation time, update exports to use that field. Backfill job for last 7 days. Running tests now. ETA EOD today.
maya: Can you also include a support playbook blurb I can send to customers (how to get CSV with local days now, and how to interpret invoices)?
samir: Yes — I'll add a short blurb and a CLI query they can run to validate counts. Example support command (for internal use):
```bash
bq query --use_legacy_sql=false "SELECT DATE(TIMESTAMP_SECONDS(event_ts) AT TIME ZONE 'Europe/Paris') as local_day, COUNT(*) FROM dataset.events WHERE org_id='org_acme_media' AND event_ts BETWEEN TIMESTAMP('2025-02-10') AND TIMESTAMP('2025-02-17') GROUP BY local_day ORDER BY local_day;"
```
That will produce per-local-day counts.

samir: Tests green on staging, pushed to staging cluster. I still need a deployment window for prod; aiming for 15:00 PST / 23:00 UTC. Backfill job scheduled to run after the roll, will create a remediation ticket linking to RI-7834.
elaine: Please add a note to the billing run team — they might need to re-run invoice generation for affected accounts or issue credits. Tagging billing: @billing-team (please evaluate impact).
maya: Noted — I'll draft a short customer message once we have ETA. For now I've told customer we're investigating and will update by EOD.
jack: Thanks everyone. @samir add estimated man-hours and rollback steps in the ticket. Also add a test case that covers org_timezones in the export pipeline.
samir: Will do. Quick note — edge cases: orgs that have DST changes will require `AT TIME ZONE org_tz` semantics and a reliable org timezone stored on org profile. We already store `org_tz` but UI wasn't used by aggregation.

maya: :thumbsup: I'll keep the support thread open with customers. Please ping me when prod deploy is done so I can update.
